THREE.js trap that cost a cycle: setting matrixWorldAutoUpdate=false on the ROOT bone only is not enough. Object3D.updateMatrixWorld recurses into children with force=true and each child with the flag still true recomputes matrixWorld from its REST offset. Must set it on EVERY bone. Symptom is a swinging weapon on a body whose bones move 0.00% relative to root.

MEASURED post-fix (browser, 60-frame light attack): drawn tip vs CombatBody.socketB = 0.0000 mm max over 60 frames on all three subjects. Guard vs socketA likewise 0.0000 mm. Identical by construction (weapon rides rig.world[gripIdx]; tip authored at local -Y*socket_b_dist_m).

HEADLINE VISUAL FINDING, only visible because the weapon is now drawn: cgs_drowned_reaper's blade tip is BELOW THE GROUND PLANE FOR EVERY FRAME OF THE SWING. tip y runs -0.83 m at rest to -1.92 m at frame 30; blade inclination runs -36.7 deg at rest to -66.3 deg at frame 30 (worsening THROUGH the swing, not just during it). Character head is at y=1.638, so the tip is up to 1.9 m below its own feet.

MECHANISM of the underground blade: MovesetLibrary._bladeLength solves CGS to 3.098 m of blade so the tip's horizontal radius equals declared reach_m 2.75. The character is ~1.75 m tall. skeleton.json's rest pose hangs the blade point-down from the hand (blade_axis_local [0,-1,0]). A 3.1 m blade hanging point-down from a hand at ~1.0 m puts the tip at -2.1 m BY ARITHMETIC. The declared reaches cannot be satisfied by a blade that also stays above ground on a 1.75 m body.

This is a DATA/solver defect, not a render defect: drawn tip == socketB to 0.0000 mm, so the renderer is faithfully drawing what hit resolution uses. Correcting it in the renderer would BREAK the what-you-see-is-what-hits-you invariant and is explicitly out of scope.
Consistent with (and worse than) the round-3 critic's numbers: they measured 35-41 deg and a tip at -1.88 m; measured here -36.7 to -66.3 deg with tip min -1.92 m and NEVER above ground.
